You're gonna have to elaborate on the fire story :p the two brands of day packs i've used are "High Sierra" and "Black wolf" both have served me well for years, in the bush and the city.

My High Sierra backpack has traveled the world with me for the past decade and still looks new. I bought it at a discount at Marshals. Think I paid $30. If their quality is still the same, I would say go for it. The way the pockets are designed is far superior to any other bag my family has, including the over priced Northface bag. The padding is excellent. My bag even has a hidden pocket and a rain cover for the bag. The laptop space is also well padded.

Edit: I found someone selling my bag used on ebay. XD

lol It comes in black. Not that I mind looking sassy. I can see why a guy wouldn't though.

Anything Osprey. Great packs all around. I highly recommend the zero gravity ones. I have a Manta 28 for my EDC. It carries great, holds more than enough stuff (including other peoples at times). Full disclosure I have only had it for a few months. But Osprey does do a lifetime warranty of the bag, even if its sold or given away, any damage to it will be fixed or the bag will be replaced. Cost me about $150.

Hidden rain fly, mesh frame, hydration reservoir included, feels great, doesn't look tacticool, about the perfect size EDC imo. The one thing I would like is more internal organization. There is some, but I would like more.

Second for Osprey. I've had their full size and day packs, (which conveniently link together) for about 5 years now. In that time I've traveled extensively and tossed them on trains, into overheads, and drug along the ground here and there. If you don't need the military addons like full MOLLE and so on they are great packs. Mine have padding on the straps as well as compartments which are great for electronics.

I upgraded from a maxpedition because I was tired of sweaty back. I really like that normys notice it less too. Its just a "normal" backpack. Not some sort of military operators pack.

Took me extensive research to decide on my pack. Will be a loyal Osprey customer for life now. Probably.

Yeah the low profile was a selling point for me too. They are quite non-descript which means less chance of being thieved. While they are well reinforced, I did add a no-cut strap to mine when I was doing some distance travel by train to make sure it stayed with me even if I dozed off.
If your looking to spend a few bucks. I would go with GoRuck, their packs will withstand a hell of a lot of torture. They run between 200 and 400.
